subject: mathematics
question_text: If A = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, B = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} and R is the relation from A to B given by x + y = 5, x ∈ A, y ∈ B, list the ordered pairs that belong to R, and find (i) the domain of R, (ii) the range of R and (iii) the codomain of R.

mark_split.label: List the pairs that satisfy x + y = 5
Write the domain, the range and the codomain

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you test each x, and what the difference is between the range and the codomain.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: List the pairs that satisfy x + y = 5
steps.margin_note: First mark. Show the line y = 5 − x, then test each x of A. The rejected value x = 0 is worth writing down.
lines: x + y = 5 gives y = 5 − x. Take each x ∈ A and keep the pair only if y ∈ B.
x = 0 → y = 5, and 5 ∉ B, so (0, 5) is rejected.
x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 → y = 4, 3, 2, 1, 0, and all of these are in B.

recall.must_convey: That y = 5 − x is tested for each x in A and only y values inside B are kept, giving five pairs.
accept: make y the subject and check each x of A against B
x equals zero gives y equals five which is not in B so it is dropped
the pairs are one four two three three two four one and five zero
y equals five minus x rasi, B lo unte matrame teesukovali
five pairs because x equals zero fails

steps.why: R is a relation from A to B, so a pair counts only when x lies in A and y lies in B. That second condition is what removes x = 0, since 5 is not a member of B.
common_mistakes: Keeping the pair (0, 5); 5 is in A but not in B, so it cannot be a second coordinate.
Reading x + y = 5 as y = x + 5.
Missing (5, 0), because 0 is wrongly thought to be outside B.
steps.memory_tip: Rearrange to y = 5 − x, then run x through A and keep only the y values that B contains.

steps.label: Write the domain, the range and the codomain
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Three separate answers are asked for, so label them (i), (ii) and (iii).
lines: Domain = the set of first members of the pairs.
Range = the set of second members of the pairs.
Codomain = B, the set the relation goes into, whether or not every member is used.

recall.must_convey: That the domain is {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, the range is {0, 1, 2, 3, 4} and the codomain is B.
accept: domain is one to five, range is zero to four, codomain is B
the codomain is the whole of B given in the question
here the range happens to fill the codomain
domain range pairs nunchi, codomain matram B ne
zero is not in the domain because x equals zero was rejected

steps.why: The codomain is the whole of B by definition, while the range is only the part of B actually reached. Here every member of B is reached, so the two sets agree, but they are answering different questions.
common_mistakes: Including 0 in the domain, when x = 0 gave no pair.
Saying the range and the codomain are always equal; they agree here only because every member of B is used.
steps.memory_tip: Domain and range are read off the pairs; the codomain is given in the question as B.
